name: Disorder of Phospholipids, Sphingolipids and Fatty Acids Biosynthesis with Peripheral Nerves Predominant Involvement
aliases: Inherited Lipid Metabolism Disorder with Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Lipid Biosynthesis Peripheral Neuropathy

criteria.description: Presence of progressive distal symmetric sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Abnormal plasma or tissue levels of phospholipids, sphingolipids, or fatty acids consistent with biosynthesis defect
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in phospholipid, sphingolipid, or fatty acid biosynthesis pathways
Electrophysiological evidence of predominantly axonal or mixed sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy
Exclusion of other common causes of peripheral neuropathy such as diabetes, toxins, or inflammatory neuropathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (clinical neuropathy, biochemical lipid abnormalities, and genetic confirmation) must be met for definitive diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by electrophysiological studies and exclusion of other neuropathies.

pathognomonic.notes: Predominantly affects lower limbs with distal weakness and sensory loss
searchTerms: nerve damage causing numbness and weakness in hands and feet
symmetrical sensory and motor nerve loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes in lower limbs
Abnormal plasma phospholipid and sphingolipid profile

common.symptomName: Muscle atrophy in distal lower limbs
searchTerms: shrinking muscles in feet and calves

common.symptomName: Paresthesias and dysesthesias in feet and hands
searchTerms: tingling and abnormal sensations in hands and feet

common.symptomName: Gait instability due to sensory loss
searchTerms: unsteady walking due to sensory loss
balance issues from sensory nerve damage

common.symptomName: Elevated serum very long chain fatty acids
searchTerms: raised very long chain fatty acids in blood
elevated long fatty acids in plasma
sensory problems in arms and hands

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal muscle weakness in upper limbs
searchTerms: mild weakness in hand and arm muscles
slight distal upper limb muscle weakness

occasional.notes: Reported in some cases possibly due to lipid metabolism abnormalities

rare.notes: Rarely reported facial weakness or sensory deficits
searchTerms: problems with facial and head nerves
nerve issues affecting face and head

laboratory: Abnormal plasma phospholipid, sphingolipid, and fatty acid profiles
Elevated very long chain fatty acids in serum
Possible mild elevation of liver enzymes
imaging: MRI neurography may show peripheral nerve enlargement or signal abnormalities
Brain MRI typically normal or nonspecific
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding enzymes involved in phospholipid, sphingolipid, or fatty acid biosynthesis (e.g., ELOVL, SPTLC1/2, AGPS)
other: Nerve conduction studies showing predominantly axonal sensorimotor neuropathy
Skin biopsy may show lipid storage abnormalities in rare cases

distinguishingFeatures: Usually caused by PMP22 duplication or mutation
Slower progression and less biochemical lipid abnormalities
Arylsulfatase A deficiency on enzyme assay
MRI showing characteristic white matter changes

redFlags: Rapidly progressive distal weakness with sensory loss
Early onset in infancy or childhood
Family history of similar neuropathy or lipid metabolism disorder
references: Orphanet: Disorder of phospholipids, sphingolipids and fatty acids biosynthesis with peripheral nerves predominant involvement - ORPHA:352309
